_comment: Example output from the Nuvra AI Planning Engine for a SaaS product.
_prompt: A landing page for a project management SaaS called 'Flow' targeting remote engineering teams. Needs pricing, testimonials, a free trial CTA, and integrations section. Professional but approachable tone.

intentSchema.rawPrompt: A landing page for a project management SaaS called 'Flow' targeting remote engineering teams. Needs pricing, testimonials, a free trial CTA, and integrations section. Professional but approachable tone.

audience.primary: Engineering managers and team leads at remote-first companies
painPoints: Lack of visibility across distributed teams

ambiguities.description: User said 'landing page' which implies a single page, but a full SaaS site typically has multiple pages.
ambiguities.suggestion: Clarify: is this a single-page marketing site or a multi-page site with About, Blog, etc.?

assumptions.reason: The mention of 'remote engineering teams' and 'project management' strongly implies a B2B SaaS context.
User specified 'landing page', interpreted as a single-page marketing site.

pages.name: Home
pages.purpose: Primary entry point — establishes value and drives free trial signups.
pages.reason: Every site requires a home page as the primary entry point and conversion surface.

sections.purpose: Provide orientation and primary navigation with a prominent free trial CTA.
sections.reason: Navigation with clear product name and primary CTA is essential for SaaS credibility.

contentIntent.headline: Communicate the Flow brand name clearly
contentIntent.body: Provide links to Features, Pricing, and Integrations sections

sections.purpose: Communicate the core job-to-be-done for remote engineering teams in one sentence.
sections.reason: Hero appears first to establish value clarity within 3 seconds — the critical window before a user decides to leave.

contentIntent.headline: Communicate that Flow eliminates the coordination overhead that slows remote engineering teams
contentIntent.body: Expand on the headline with a specific, concrete benefit — not a feature list

sections.purpose: Reduce skepticism immediately after the hero with recognizable company logos or a key metric.
sections.reason: Quantified results immediately after the hero establish credibility for a SaaS product.

contentIntent.body: Show logos of 4-6 recognizable companies using Flow, or a single compelling metric (e.g., '10,000+ engineering teams')

sections.purpose: Detail the specific capabilities that matter most to remote engineering teams.
sections.reason: Feature overview gives technical evaluators the information they need.

contentIntent.headline: Communicate that Flow is purpose-built for how engineering teams actually work
contentIntent.body: Highlight 3-4 features that directly address the pain points of remote engineering teams: visibility, async communication, and integration with developer tools

sections.purpose: Reduce perceived onboarding effort by showing the path from signup to first value.
sections.reason: SaaS products require onboarding clarity — users need to understand the workflow before committing.

contentIntent.headline: Communicate that getting started with Flow is fast and does not require a long setup
contentIntent.body: Show 3 steps: connect your tools, invite your team, start tracking. Each step should take less than 2 minutes.

sections.purpose: Signal ecosystem maturity and reduce switching cost concerns for engineering teams.
sections.reason: Integration ecosystem signals maturity and reduces switching cost concerns — explicitly requested by the user.

contentIntent.headline: Communicate that Flow works with the tools engineering teams already use
contentIntent.body: Show logos of key integrations: GitHub, Jira, Slack, Linear, Figma, etc.

sections.purpose: Build trust through specific, credible stories from engineering managers at recognizable companies.
sections.reason: Customer stories from recognizable companies provide social proof for B2B buyers — explicitly requested by the user.

contentIntent.headline: Communicate that real engineering teams have achieved measurable results with Flow
contentIntent.body: Show 2-3 testimonials from engineering managers. Each should include a specific, quantified outcome (e.g., '40% fewer status meetings').

sections.purpose: Present pricing transparently to remove the #1 objection for B2B SaaS buyers.
sections.reason: Transparent pricing is a trust signal for SaaS — hiding it creates friction. Explicitly requested by the user.

contentIntent.headline: Communicate that Flow has a plan for every team size, with a free trial available
contentIntent.body: Show 3 plans: Free (up to 5 users), Pro (per seat), Enterprise (custom). Highlight the Pro plan as recommended.

sections.purpose: Address the most common objections and questions that block B2B engineering teams from starting a trial.
sections.reason: FAQ addresses technical and contractual questions that block B2B decisions.

contentIntent.headline: Address the questions engineering managers ask before starting a trial
contentIntent.body: Cover: data security and compliance, migration from existing tools, team onboarding time, and support options.

sections.purpose: Create a clear, low-friction path to starting a free trial for users who have read the full page.
sections.reason: Closing CTA captures high-intent users who have read through the full page.

contentIntent.headline: Communicate that starting a free trial is risk-free and takes less than 2 minutes
contentIntent.body: Reinforce the free trial offer with a guarantee (no credit card required, cancel anytime).

sections.purpose: Provide navigation fallback, legal information, and trust signals.
sections.reason: Footer with security badges and compliance links is critical for B2B trust.

contentIntent.body: Include links to Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, and Security page. Add SOC 2 and GDPR compliance badges.
